Subject: Request: baseline embed rates + dimension limits

Hi Rafael,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We are putting together a short evaluation to compare embedding economics across vendors and have a few concrete asks so we can model unit costs:

- Baseline hosted API rates (per-vector or per-1k vectors) for the commonly-used dimensionalities you support (768, 1536, 2048). If you have the canonical model name next to each (e.g., redwood-embed-large-v1) that helps.
- Do you map anything to per-token billing for embeddings (i.e., are there token-based charges that get applied before vectors are returned)?
- Is there a dimensionality premium (e.g., higher $/vector for >1536 dims) or is pricing flat per vector regardless of length?
- Bulk discount tiers / committed spend thresholds you typically offer for embeddings.
- Any limits on per-request dimension sizes or per-account vector throughput (QPS / sustained vectors per minute)?
- Does Redwood accept variable-dimension payloads within the same index/ingest job, or do you require a fixed dimension per index?

I attached a simple rate-request spreadsheet with our expected monthly vector distribution (by dim). Can you and your pricing/solutions folks confirm?

We have a deadline to finalize vendor economics this coming Friday — ideally a short call tomorrow or Thursday to align.

Best,
Samira

Hi Samira — thanks for the spreadsheet, this is very clear. Quick answers up front, followed by a short summary and next steps.

Summary (baseline hosted API public list rates):
- redwood-embed-small-v1 (768) — $0.00020 per vector (per call result)
- redwood-embed-large-v1 (1536) — $0.00035 per vector
- redwood-embed-xl-v1 (2048) — $0.00050 per vector

Notes:
- We bill embeddings per-vector returned by the model. There is no additional per-token charge on the hosted embeddings endpoint — the tokenization happens in the model pipeline but the invoiceable unit is the vector.
- Dimension premium: up to 1536 is our baseline; dims above 1536 (2048 in our current catalog) carry a modest premium as above. We do accept arbitrary dimension payloads in Private/Dedicated setups but for hosted API the models available today are the three listed.
- Variable-dimension payloads: hosted API expects you to pick the model (and thus dimension) per request. Mixing dimensionalities in the same index is supported at the application layer but not recommended for similarity scoring without down/up projection — we usually advise normalizing to a single model/dimension per index.
- Rate limits / throughput: default hosted quotas are 1,000 vectors/sec account-wide burstable; sustained throughput guaranteed on Dedicated. We can support higher sustained rates with a Dedicated or Reserved commit.

Volume discounts (hosted API, tiered):
- 10% off list at >= 10M vectors/month
- 20% off list at >= 50M vectors/month
- Custom pricing for committed contracts (we typically evaluate at $75k+/month committed embedding spend)

Attached a short baseline spreadsheet (Redwood_embed_baseline_20261202.xlsx) that mirrors the numbers above and includes an example cost model for your sample distribution.

Next steps:
1) If you can share a 30–90 day expected vector run rate and the % split by dim from your attached sheet, Ben (cc'd) can produce a committed vs. pay-as-you-go pro forma.
2) Lauren (cc'd) can walk through technical fit — especially around indexing and dimension normalization.
3) Happy to do a 30-minute call tomorrow (Thu) 10–11am PT; if that works I can send a calendar invite.

Hope this helps — we can tighten numbers once we see your month-to-month profile.

Best,
Rafael Mendes

Thanks Rafael — helpful summary. A couple quick clarifications before we run numbers:

- You say "per-vector returned" — does that mean if we request 3 different prompts for the same record and deduplicate later in our pipeline, we are charged for 3 vectors? Or does Redwood offer any server-side dedupe/caching (prefix or exact) that would reduce billable units?
- For the dimension premium: do you prorate price by dimension size (e.g., 1536 -> baseline, 2048 -> 1536 * 1.33) or is it a discrete price per model as you listed?
- We have a small segment (about 8% of vectors) that are 384-d from a legacy embedding model. Can we send mixed dims in a single bulk ingest call or do we need to split?

If we can get simple answers to those three, we'll run your pro forma vs. the other vendors. Also, is there any short-term promotional credit for new customers doing a POC?

—Samira

From: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
To: Samira Qureshi <samira.qureshi@nexify.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 13:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: baseline embed rates + dimension limits

Samira — quick answers inline: 

- Dedup/caching: hosted API performs exact-match caching for identical input payloads when cache headers are enabled; that will reduce billable vectors because the cached result is returned without executing the model. Client-side dedupe is still the most predictable approach. For Dedicated/Private, we offer prefix and KV caching options that can further reduce model execution charges for repeated prefixes.

- Dimension pricing: discrete by model. The per-vector prices I shared are the invoiceable units per model; we do not prorate linearly by dimension size. For non-catalog dims (e.g., 384) the hosted API will accept them only if you call a model that produces that dim. For mixed-dimension payloads sent to hosted endpoints we treat each request independently — you can mix calls in a single bulk job but costs are computed per-response vector. If you want to store mixed dims in a single index, you will need to handle projection/normalization; Lauren can help with options (down-projection, PCA, or re-embedding).

- Promo: we offer a $15k new-customer POC credit for qualified accounts (applies to hosted usage for 30 days) — subject to a quick technical call and an NDA.

Ben will take point on the pro forma once you share the monthly mix. Lauren — could you prepare a short note on recommended approaches for indexing mixed-dimension historical data?

I'll send a calendar invite for Thu 10am PT unless you reply with a different time.

Thanks — Rafael
